Beat 'niche' ('12 m: the bottom. A niche the Church holds to be Saint Peter's grave.') puts St Peter's niche at 12 m, the deepest point. Wikipedia gives only a 5-12 m range for the whole necropolis and Turismo Roma does not give the tomb's depth; the topic's verify list says exactly this: say the necropolis reaches 12 m, not that Peter's tomb is at 12 m. Fix: separate the two, e.g. '12 m: the necropolis's lowest point.' and then 'And in it, a niche the Church holds to be Saint Peter's grave.' (no depth on the niche; the 'deepest' tag/label must not sit on the niche either).

Beat 'nave' ('10 m, under the nave: 22 tombs.') reads as 22 tombs at 10 m under the nave. Wikipedia's 22 is the count of excavated tombs in the whole necropolis (5-12 m), not at that level. Fix the wording, e.g. '10 m, under the nave. Archaeologists have dug out 22 tombs.' and keep the TOMBS FOUND counter from implying it counts one level.

Confirmed: 5 m and 12 m (Wikipedia, 'depths varying between 5 and 12 metres'), 22 excavated tombs and more than 1,000 funerals (Wikipedia), about 10 m under the central nave (turismoroma.it page, fetched), Constantine buried the street to level the ground for his basilica (Wikipedia), popes buried in the Grottoes (Wikipedia Vatican Grottoes, National Geographic via search). 'Held to be' wording for the grave is right. Grottoes shown without a depth (the 3 m is a travel guide only), good. Hook avoids 'biggest church'. Description ends with the channel disclaimer.
